FILED s407 (Fable, drop-harvest sizing â docs/option-b-phase2-plan.md Track C).
perl: `~~$y` where a TERM is expected is `~(~$y)` (bop.t asserts is(~~$y, 3));
PPI 1.291: PPI::Token::Operator '~~' â always the smartmatch operator, so PCL's
main loop sees a binary operator with no left operand and the statement is
DROPPED ("Fell through. Missing case").  2 drops in each population (bop.t:196,
bop.t:285).
FIX: the token-stream repair family (Parser2 _repair_*): an Operator '~~' whose
previous significant token does NOT end a term (_ends_term, s407-amended to
know method-name Words) is split into two Operator '~' tokens; the INFIX `~~`
(smartmatch, after a term) is left alone (Track A refuses it perl-shaped).
Both lists in the commit: fires (`print ~~$y`, `is(~~$y, 3)`, `f(~~$x)`),
must-NOT-fire (`$a ~~ $b`, `$a ~~ @list`, `$h{k} ~~ 1`, `$o->m ~~ 1`).
RULE 13 obligations in the SAME commit: docs/ppi-upstream-bugs.md section
(minimal repro, dump vs expected, PPI version), docs/ppi-bug-report.t row
(bump tests => N), canary in Pl/t/misc-fixes-02.t.

DONE s415 (commit s415c).  Parser2::_repair_term_initial_complement splits a
`~~` whose previous significant token fails _ends_term into two `~` tokens and
reparses; an infix one is untouched and #371 refuses it perl-shaped.  Rule 13
obligations in the same commit: docs/ppi-upstream-bugs.md Â§21, bug 20 in
docs/ppi-bug-report.t (tests => 20, FAILS on 1.291 as it should), and three
behaviour rows plus the CANARY in Pl/t/misc-fixes-02.t.
The #371 refusal classifier stopped re-asking the infix question with its own
whitelist -- it had missed `$o->method ~~ 1` (probed: dropped instead of
refusing).  One predicate, upstream.
